sections.content: You know *antes de* from A1 Unit 7 and the *pretérito perfecto* from Unit 1. Put them together: the *pretérito perfecto* says what you have done, and *antes de* + infinitive names the action that comes later. The infinitive does not change for the subject. With a reflexive verb such as *lavarse*, the pronoun comes before *he*, *has*, *ha*… as it does before any conjugated verb: *Me he lavado las manos*, *Nos hemos lavado las manos*.

items.spanish: Me he lavado las manos antes de empezar.
items.english: I have washed my hands before starting.

items.spanish: Hemos preparado los ingredientes antes de cocinar.
items.english: We have prepared the ingredients before cooking.

items.spanish: Carlos ha cortado las verduras antes de empezar.
items.english: Carlos has cut the vegetables before starting.

items.spanish: Se han lavado las manos antes de ponerse el delantal.
items.english: They have washed their hands before putting on the apron.

sections.content: When the same person does both actions, *antes de* is followed by the bare infinitive, just like English 'before starting': *antes de empezar* covers *yo*, *tú* or *ellos* without changing.
